title: Adjective Declension 3: Genitive Singular
description: The genitive singular for hard-stem adjectives. The masculine and neuter share -ого. The feminine has -ой. The same endings cover possession (у меня нет ...), absence, and the prepositions из / у / без / для / от.
descriptionRussian: Родительный падеж единственного числа: мужской и средний делят окончание -ого; женский -ой. Эти окончания работают для отрицания (у меня нет ...), отсутствия и предлогов из / у / без / для / от.
intro: This is where the merge starts. From here to the end of the singular, masculine and neuter take the same ending in every case. The feminine begins a run of its own at the same time: the form you learn today will still be the right one three lessons from now. Two columns, and one of them barely moves.
rules: Masculine and neuter share one genitive singular ending: -ого. Hard-stem -ый and -ое both become -ого in the genitive. Spelled -ого, pronounced /-ovo/.
Feminine takes -ой in the genitive singular. Hard-stem -ая becomes -ой. The same -ой will return for the feminine dative, instrumental, and prepositional.
The genitive triggers that govern nouns also govern their adjectives: у меня нет ...; нет ...; без / для / из / от / у + gen; numbers 5+ + gen pl. Adjective and noun move together.
The masculine and neuter merge from the genitive onward through the prepositional. The feminine has its own pair (-ой across four cases). The plural collapses gender entirely (Lesson 7).
examples: У меня нет нового журнала. (I don't have a new magazine.) Журнал is masc; nominative нового → genitive нового, журнал → журнала.
У меня нет новой книги. (I don't have a new book.) Книга is fem; новая → новой, книга → книги.
У меня нет нового письма. (I don't have a new letter.) Письмо is neut; новое → нового. Same ending as masculine.
Маша выходит из старого парка. (Masha is leaving the old park.) 'Из + gen': старый → старого, парк → парка.
Антон не пьёт холодной воды. (Anton doesn't drink cold water.) 'Нет' takes gen: холодная → холодной, вода → воды.
Это подарок для умной сестры. (This is a present for the smart sister.) 'Для + gen': умная → умной, сестра → сестры.

items.hint: Recap from Lesson 2: брат is masculine animate. What does the accusative do?
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 2. Брат is masculine animate, so the accusative borrows the genitive form: нового. Today's lesson teaches the same -ого as the genitive proper: нового брата would also be 'нет нового брата.' Same ending, two roles.

items.promptEnglish: I don't have a new magazine.
items.hint: Журнал is masculine. The nominative -ый becomes which ending in the genitive?
items.explanation: Журнал is masculine. The masculine genitive ending is -ого: нового. Notice the spelling-vs-pronunciation note: write нового, say /novovo/. The trigger 'у меня нет' is a textbook genitive cue; the adjective and the noun both move.

items.promptEnglish: I don't have a new book.
items.hint: Книга is feminine. The feminine genitive ending is brand new today.
items.explanation: Книга is feminine. The feminine genitive ending is -ой: новой. -ой will return as the feminine ending for the dative, instrumental, and prepositional too; locking it now pays off across the next three lessons.

items.promptEnglish: Anton is leaving the old park.
items.hint: Парк is masculine. 'Из' triggers which case?
items.explanation: 'Из + gen' triggers the genitive. Парк is masculine, so старый → старого. The pattern of from-where motion (Russian Q: 'Откуда?') always wants the genitive.

items.promptEnglish: This is a gift for the smart sister.
items.hint: Сестра is feminine. Apply the new -ой ending.
items.explanation: 'Для + gen' triggers the genitive. Сестра is feminine, so умная → умной. The phrase 'для умной сестры' recurs in Q2.3 of the FIB; you may already feel the pattern setting.

items.promptEnglish: I don't have a new lake.
items.hint: Озеро is neuter. Does the neuter take its own ending or share with another slot?
items.explanation: Озеро is neuter. From the genitive onward, neuter shares its ending with masculine. -ое becomes -ого: нового. The same form covers a masculine inanimate (нового парка), masculine animate (нового брата as direct object), and neuter (нового письма).

blanks: Антон не пьёт _____ воды. (Anton doesn't drink cold water.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: 'Не пить + gen' (the negated 'drink' verb takes a genitive object). Вода is feminine, so холодная → холодной. The same -ой also marks 'пить без холодной воды' or 'нет холодной воды'.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha doesn't have an interesting magazine.
errorCorrection.explanation: 'У ... нет' is a genitive trigger, so both the noun and its adjective go into the genitive: журнала and интересного. The masculine -ый becomes -ого (spelled -ого, pronounced /-ovo/). Интересный is the nominative form.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha came out of the old school.
errorCorrection.explanation: 'Из + genitive' triggers the genitive, so школа becomes школы and the adjective takes the feminine genitive -ой: старой. Старую is the feminine ACCUSATIVE (Я вижу старую школу), an easy slip because both are oblique forms.

errorCorrection.sentence: Рядом с городом нет красивое озера.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: There is no beautiful lake near the city.
errorCorrection.explanation: Нет is a genitive trigger, and from the genitive onward the neuter shares the masculine ending: -ое becomes -ого, giving красивого озера. Красивое is the nominative/accusative neuter form, correct when the lake is the subject (Красивое озеро далеко). Because the neuter -ое and the noun's -о look alike, learners often leave the adjective unchanged, but the genitive moves it to -ого.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I don't have an interesting magazine.
minimalPairs.explanation: 'Нет + gen' triggers the genitive. Журнал is masculine, so интересный → интересного. Интересный would only be correct in the nominative (the subject of a sentence) or the masculine inanimate accusative.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Masha is leaving the small room.
minimalPairs.explanation: 'Из + gen' triggers the genitive. Комната is feminine, so маленькая → маленькой. Маленькая would be correct only in the nominative.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each adjective form by its genitive slot.

reviewVocab.definition: genitive case (marks absence, possession, source of motion, and the object of many prepositions; answers 'Кого? / Чего?')
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'У меня нет нового журнала' слова 'нового' и 'журнала' стоят в родительном падеже.

reviewVocab.definition: absence (the meaning of 'у меня нет ...'; the noun and its adjective both go into the genitive)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'У Антона нет новой книги' конструкция 'у ... нет' выражает отсутствие.

reviewVocab.definition: out of, from (preposition + genitive; source of motion or origin)
reviewVocab.example: В фразе 'из старого парка' предлог 'из' требует родительного падежа: старый → старого, парк → парка.
